newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba premier says possible flood top issue.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba premier says possible flood top issue.

text.p: Manitoba Premier Gary Filmon said on Thursday likely spring flooding was the most pressing problem currently facing his province.
"It's probably the most pressing issue that we face in Manitoba today. The flood waters are rapidly rising and we're expecting substantial damage and substantial cost to Manitoba," he told reporters.
Standing at Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien's side after signing a labor training agreement, he said they had discussed the flood problem.

"There's a strong and firm commitment by federal government to be there when we need them under the normal formula for support financially as well as, if necessary, resources for instance from Defense and so on to be available to us," Filmon said.
Chretien said Defense Minister Doug Young had confirmed to him that everything that could be done would be done.
"The Canadian Army is preparing for that unfortunate situation that will come within days," he said.
